Aisha: quick summary from the bring-up benches for redwood-open-7b-q4 (quantized)
Aisha: ran end-to-end p95/throughput sweep across H100 (us-west1) and A100 (eu-west1). goal: size Dedicated pools for GA with p95 < 250ms for chat workloads and ~20% autoscale headroom.
Aisha: short results (see CSV below). looking for opinions on concurrency targets and autoscaler headroom before I put this in the runbook.
Aisha: ```
gpu,region,concurrency,p95_ms,throughput_tok_s,cost_hour
H100,us-west1,1,120,650,3.6
H100,us-west1,4,210,2200,3.6
H100,us-west1,8,380,3800,3.6
A100,eu-west1,1,140,580,2.9
A100,eu-west1,4,260,1900,2.9
A100,eu-west1,6,410,2600,2.9
```
Aisha: notes: quantized path reduces tokens/sec variance but increases p95 at higher conc due to kernel scheduling. H100 > A100 for high-conc throughput but p95 climbs past 250ms around conc=6.
Ben: thanks — nice bench. my two cents:
Ben: target per-GPU concurrency = 4 for steady state (keeps p95 below target). allow burst up to conc=8 per GPU but only if latency SLO can be relaxed for best-effort routes.
Ben: autoscaler headroom = 25% of committed capacity; that lets us absorb short traffic spikes without cold-starts. for scheduled bursts (campaigns) plan reserved extra nodes.
Diego: +1 on 25% headroom. also remember node packing: our smallest Dedicated node is 8x H100. so 1 node = 8 GPUs — sizing should be in node units.
Diego: propose min commit = 2 nodes (16 GPUs) per region for HA, baseline concurrency 4 -> effective concurrency capacity = 16 * 4 = 64 concurrent sessions.
Cassie: cost check: what's the hourly delta if we pick 2 nodes vs 3 nodes in us-west1? need to show to finance before we lock commit.
Aisha: rough cost delta in bench CSV is per-GPU. so 2 nodes (16 GPUs @ H100): ~16 * 3.6 = $57.6/hr; 3 nodes ~= $86.4/hr. (approx)
Cassie: OK thanks, that's helpful. can we model 95th p95 impact if we force conc=6 steady instead of 4? we need to show latency-risk vs cost savings.
Ben: short answer: conc=6 drops cost per session but p95 for H100 moved to ~380ms in the bench (above SLO). so we'd need fallback routing to cheaper model variants for SLO-critical traffic or reserve extra GPUs.
Aisha: suggestion for runbook entry:
Aisha: - baseline: commit 2 nodes (16 H100) per region
Aisha: - steady concurrency target: 4 per GPU
Aisha: - autoscale headroom: 25% (scale out triggers at 75% utilization)
Aisha: - burst/temporary capacity: let autoscaler spin up 1 extra node (8 GPUs) for scheduled campaigns, fallback to redwood-open-3b for SLO-critical routes if p95 > 300ms
Aisha: include kernel note: for quantized q4 we saw better throughput with the custom fused attention kernels on H100; fallback to default kernels on A100 to avoid regressions.
Diego: one operational caveat — when autoscaler adds nodes we need warm-up time (~45-60s) for the KV cache to fill; for chat flows that can show a p99 spike. consider prefix-caching for critical customers.
perf-bot: automated report: perf dashboard update: https://perf.redwood.internal/bench/1766123456 — regression detected in quantized-scheduled-run: p95 increased by 18% in eu-west1 between run A and run B :warning:
Aisha: noted — I'll re-run the quantized kernel sweep overnight with extended sequence lengths (2k) and post results tomorrow. will also add a quick A/B for the fused kernel toggles.
Cassie: :thumbsup: thanks, sounds like a good plan. once you have the overnight numbers can we produce a cost/latency sensitivity chart for the customer-facing doc?
Aisha: yep, will produce a small table + chart and ping growth/product. aiming to have a PR for runbook by EOD tomorrow.
Ben: thanks — one more ask: include a simple scaling policy snippet we can drop into the Dedicated config (scaleOutThreshold=0.75, coolDown=60s, maxBurstNodes=1).
Aisha: will add that. cc @Diego for node packing constraints when we write the Terraform bits.
Diego: got it. I'll hold off on node launch templates until we lock kernel options.
Aisha: thanks all. rolling this into the eng-platform sizing doc after the overnight runs.
